inference in·fer·ence | ˈinf(ə)rəns | noun a conclusion reached on the basis of evidence and reasoning: researchers are entrusted with drawing inferences from the data | it seemed a fair inference that such books would be grouped together. • the process of inferring something: his emphasis on order and health, and by inference cleanliness. ORIGIN late 16th century: from medieval Latin inferentia, from inferent- ‘bringing in’, from the verb inferre (see infer).
